# RV power station and solar combos

No single combo wins for every RV. The right pick depends on whether you need to run a roof A/C. A 13,500 BTU unit draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup, so you need a station with at least that much surge headroom ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

## My picks

**1. Best for A/C and full-time boondocking: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, expandable past 12kWh.
- About 0-80% in roughly 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- It's heavy (a two-person lift) and the most expensive option once you add batteries.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). The article doesn't give a price, so check current pricing before you buy.

**2. Best value for big capacity: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456Wh LiFePO4, 3,600W at 120V (6,000W peak), a dedicated RV outlet and a 5-year warranty.
- Accepts up to 2,000W of solar across three inputs, each capped at 650W. You need panels on all three to hit 2,000W.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's more of a "stays in the RV" unit.
- Store price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200, expires 2026-11-15) brings it to $1,319.12, according to [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh).
- Sale items can't be returned, and the checkout has the final word on the code.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.

**3. Mid-range with a 30A RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W, up to 1,200W solar input, about 62 lb ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- It's a good fit for fridge, lights and electronics. It won't comfortably start a large A/C.
- Don't confuse it with the older AC200P, which has only 700W solar input and a 2-year warranty ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)).

**4. Lighter weekend setup: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 or EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- The Jackery is 1,070Wh and 23.8 lb, with a 400W solar ceiling, and pairs with two SolarSaga 200W panels.
- The DELTA 3 Plus is 1,024Wh and 1,800W, with up to 1,000W solar input and expansion to 5kWh ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

## Solar panels

- **Match the panels to the station's solar input limit.** A big array on a station with a low ceiling is wasted ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)).
- **A 300-400W folding array** can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of good sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- **Jackery** works best with its own SolarSaga panels, and 2×200W uses the full 400W.
- **A budget option** mentioned in one guide is the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).
- **Check connectors and voltage range** before buying panels from a different brand.

## Caveats

- Apart from the ALLPOWERS link, the search results only gave me review pages, not direct product pages. I didn't want to guess at product URLs. The review pages have "check price" buttons, but those are mostly Amazon affiliate links.
- Many of these guides are affiliate-driven, and prices vary between sources, so confirm specs and price at checkout.
- Plugging into an existing outlet or shore-power adapter is simple. Any permanent wiring into the RV should be done by a qualified electrician.

If you tell me your RV's biggest loads (especially whether you have a roof A/C), how many nights you boondock, and your budget, I can narrow this to one station and a specific panel size.
